title: NIST Research Data Framework (RDaF) Version 2.0
what: Six-stage cyclical research-data lifecycle; definitions, cross-cutting themes, quality as fit-for-purpose, provenance and chain-of-custody.

title: DCC Curation Lifecycle Model
what: Data-centric curation model showing continuous description, preservation planning, community watch and curation across the lifecycle.

title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship
what: Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable principles; persistent identifiers, rich metadata, access protocols, provenance, licenses and domain standards.

title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
what: Interchange model for provenance using entities, activities and agents; designed to be specialized by domains.

title: ISO 14721:2025 — Reference Model for an Open Archival Information System (OAIS)
what: Long-term preservation reference model; ingest, archival storage, data management, access, preservation planning, designated community and representation information.

title: PREMIS Data Dictionary for Preservation Metadata
what: Core preservation metadata model for objects, events, agents, rights and associated preservation evidence.

title: DataCite Metadata Schema
what: Current generic citation/discovery metadata schema for research outputs; includes identifiers, creators, versions, related identifiers and resource types.

title: Levels of Digital Preservation
what: Practical maturity guidance around storage, integrity, control, metadata and content; v2.1 adds environmental sustainability guidance.

title: CoreTrustSeal Trustworthy Data Repositories Requirements
what: Current requirements for trustworthy repositories, covering organizational infrastructure, digital object management and technology/security.

title: The TRUST Principles for digital repositories
what: Transparency, Responsibility, User focus, Sustainability and Technology for trustworthy repositories; complements FAIR.

title: Reproducibility and Replicability in Science
what: Defines computational reproducibility as obtaining consistent results using the same data, methods, code and analysis conditions; distinguishes replication using new data.

title: International Vocabulary of Metrology (VIM) — JCGM 200:2012
what: Definitions of measurement, calibration, measurement uncertainty and metrological traceability; traceability does not by itself guarantee fitness for purpose.

title: Final NIH Policy for Data Management and Sharing
what: Requires a Data Management and Sharing Plan for covered NIH research and emphasizes responsible data management, preservation and appropriate sharing.

title: Selecting a Data Repository
what: Desirable repository characteristics: PID, sustainability, metadata, curation/QA, provenance, retention, access controls and long-term management.

title: What FAIR is not
what: FAIR is not a standard, not equivalent to open, and does not itself cover intrinsic data quality or ethics.

title: RO-Crate Metadata Specification
what: Current recommendation for packaging research data with machine-readable JSON-LD metadata, contextual entities, provenance and workflow descriptions.

title: The Availability of Research Data Declines Rapidly with Article Age
what: In 516 studies aged 2–22 years, odds of a dataset being reported extant fell by 17% per year; illustrates fragility of researcher-only long-term stewardship.

title: Gene name errors are widespread in the scientific literature
what: In selected genomics journals, 19.6% of papers with supplementary Excel gene lists were affected by gene-name conversion errors; illustrates silent transformation risk.

title: Scholarly Context Not Found: One in Five Articles Suffers from Reference Rot
what: Large-scale study found one in five STM articles suffered reference rot; among articles containing web references, seven in ten were affected.

title: Digital Preservation Handbook — Storage
what: Explains why backup and digital preservation are not the same and why long-term preservation adds integrity monitoring, redundancy, planning and active stewardship.

title: NOMAD MetaInfo / computational data documentation
what: Structured machine-readable computational materials metadata organized around method, system, calculation and workflow information.

title: OPTIMADE Specification
what: Common REST API and schemas for interoperable access to materials databases, including structures and optional calculations/files/references.
